title: The Last Cipher
premise: Ines Galloway, a concierge at the fading Hotel Verity, has spent a lifetime observing guests without being observed. When long-term resident Marisol Vega vanishes, Ines finds her diary in the lost-and-found—entries continuing for three weeks after her disappearance, written in handwriting that isn't quite hers. As Ines deciphers the coded entries, they realize someone is staging Marisol's life to frame a dead man, and that the killer is feeding details from the police file back into the diary. The trail leads to a decades-old wrongful conviction that several powerful guests helped bury. Ines must lay a trap using the hotel itself as bait, exposing the killer—a retired detective who wrote the original case file—before the statute of limitations erases Marisol's last chance at justice.
about_author: Kestrel Ashgrove spent eleven years working night desks in grand old hotels before turning to crime fiction, and their novels are known for elevators, lobbies, and stairwells as places where secrets change hands. They live above a bookshop in a coastal city and claim they can read a guest's whole biography from their luggage.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unclaimed Luggage
chapters.summary: Ines Galloway's POV. A quiet Tuesday shift establishes Ines's gift: reading guests through small details—their shoes, their lies, their tipping habits. Marisol Vega, a reclusive long-term resident on the fourth floor, asks Ines to hold a package 'until I ask for it.' The beat is unease: Marisol looks frightened in a way Ines has learned not to name.

chapters.title: Room 412, Do Not Disturb
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Marisol misses checkout by two days; housekeeping finds the room immaculate, bed unslept, and no forwarding address. Police take a routine report and leave quickly. Ines notices what they don't: Marisol's reading glasses left behind, though she never went anywhere without them. The emotional beat is the first crack in Ines's practiced detachment.

chapters.title: Lost and Found
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Sorting unclaimed items, Ines finds Marisol's diary in a locked drawer of the front desk—somewhere it was never logged in. The final entry is dated nine days after her disappearance. Ines tells themselves it's a clerical error, but reads on anyway. The beat is complicity: curiosity overriding the professional rule of never getting involved.

chapters.title: A Handwriting Almost Her Own
chapters.summary: Ines POV, with diary excerpts. The post-disappearance entries describe ordinary days—breakfast, rain, a phone call—but small details are wrong: the hotel's lobby clock described as digital, tea where Marisol drank coffee. Someone is impersonating her life on paper. Ines feels watched for the first time in years. Beat: fear disguised as fascination.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Deciphering Marisol's margin codes—developed, Ines realizes, during her years as a court stenographer—the diary reveals names hidden inside mundane entries: judges, businessmen, all former guests of the Verity. One name recurs: Aldous Renner, convicted of murder twenty-five years ago, died in prison. Beat: the thrill of translation curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Detective Okafor Returns
chapters.summary: Detective Nnamdi Okafor POV. The missing persons case is reopened when Marisol's sister files formally. Okafor, who worked the original Renner case as a young officer, interviews Ines and notices the diary is missing from evidence intake—or never arrived. He doesn't say so. Beat: two careful people measuring each other across a desk.

chapters.title: What the File Says
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. Reviewing the cold case file, he finds the Renner conviction rested on testimony from four witnesses—all connected to the Verity—and a confession extracted under circumstances he's spent his career not examining. Someone has recently accessed the archived file; the log shows a retired badge number. Beat: institutional loyalty beginning to rot.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Cross-referencing the diary's names against the hotel's ancient ledger books, Ines discovers all four original witnesses stayed at the Verity the same week, arranged by one booking: E. Halloran. Ines remembers him—now a frail, charming regular who tips extravagantly and asks oddly precise questions about staff routines. Beat: the hunter realizing he's been studied.

chapters.title: Tea with Mr. Halloran
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Halloran invites Ines for tea and probes, gently, about the diary, about Marisol's habits, about whether Ines 'notices things.' Ines performs obliviousness while cataloguing every tell. He mentions, casually, the exact date the statute of limitations expires. Beat: a duel conducted entirely in pleasantries.

chapters.title: Nine Days After
chapters.summary: Ines POV, interleaved with diary entries. Re-reading the forged entries, Ines spots the pattern: each contains one true detail only someone with case-file access would know—the contents of Marisol's trash, the position of her suitcase. The forger isn't just faking her survival; he's rehearsing an alibi, building a record that she left town alive. Beat: understanding arriving like cold water.

chapters.title: The Stenographer's Last Transcript
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The cipher's deepest layer decodes to a partial transcript: Marisol had been secretly transcribing a deathbed confession from one of the witnesses, implicating Halloran—then a rising detective—in framing Renner. She wasn't hiding from Halloran; she was documenting him. Beat: grief for a stranger becoming personal mission.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. He pulls the retirement records: E. Halloran is Edmund Halloran, the lead detective on the Renner case, now living comfortably off a pension and consulting fees. Okafor requests the statute timeline and is stonewalled by a captain who owes Halloran favors. Beat: choosing between career and conscience.

chapters.title: The Fourth Floor Is Closed
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Halloran checks into the Verity again under a new name, taking the room directly below 412. Housekeeping reports his room smells faintly of bleach; his luggage includes a document scanner. He's finishing something. Ines realizes the diary was planted for Ines to find—Halloran wants a witness to Marisol's fictional departure. Beat: being moved like a piece on a board.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Amateurs
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ines approaches Okafor off the record with the diary; Okafor admits the file access log. Neither fully trusts the other, but they agree: Halloran must be caught acting, not suspected. Okafor warns that anything Ines touches becomes tainted evidence. Beat: wary partnership sealed over bad coffee in the hotel kitchen.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Studying surveillance instincts honed over decades, Ines maps Halloran's routine: he walks the fourth-floor corridor nightly at 11:40, testing doors. Ines learns Marisol's transcript is incomplete—one witness's page is missing, likely hidden in the hotel, which explains why Halloran keeps returning. Beat: patience sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Following Marisol's cipher reference to 'the register,' Ines finds the final page sewn inside the spine of the hotel's oldest guest ledger: the full confession naming Halloran, plus Marisol's note that she'd mailed a copy to herself for safekeeping—if it still exists. Beat: triumph immediately shadowed by the knowledge that finding it makes Ines a target.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. With five days left, Okafor's warrant request is denied; the captain suggests he take leave. Okafor goes around him, quietly contacting the original case's disgraced junior officer, now a private investigator, who confirms Halloran coached all four witnesses. Beat: the law revealing itself as another room Halloran holds a key to.

chapters.title: Eleven Forty
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The trap: Ines lets slip to Halloran that the 'lost' ledger is being sent to archival restoration tomorrow—forcing him to act tonight. Ines waits in the dark of the archive room, heart hammering, as footsteps stop at 11:40 precisely. Beat: terror held perfectly still.

chapters.title: The Confession Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. Halloran breaks in and finds the ledger wired to Okafor's recorder; Ines steps out of the shadows and recites, verbatim, everything Halloran has said and done since check-in—every tell Ines catalogued. Halloran lunges; Okafor intervenes; the arrest happens on hotel property, witnessed by staff Ines quietly assembled. Beat: invisibility weaponized.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. Under interrogation, Halloran confesses to Marisol's murder and the Renner frame, believing the statute protects the old crime—it doesn't, because the conspiracy continued. The mailed copy of the transcript surfaces at a defunct post office, corroborating everything. Beat: justice arriving through paperwork, which is its own kind of poetry.

chapters.title: Checkout
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The Verity fills with reporters; Ines deflects them all, giving Okafor the credit and keeping the diary out of the story. Marisol's sister collects her belongings and thanks Ines for noticing what no one else did. Ines returns to the desk, the lobby quieter than before. Beat: sorrow braided with earned peace.

chapters.title: The Next Guest
chapters.summary: Ines POV, closing. Weeks later, a new long-term guest arrives with nervous eyes and too many locks on her luggage. Ines watches her cross the lobby and recognizes the posture of someone running. This time, Ines writes down the room number unprompted and slides it, later, to Okafor. Beat: the observer choosing, finally, to be seen.
